narrative:
The model predicts a 75% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability means the system sees strong signs that you are likely to depart in the near future.

Three factors stood out most in this decision. First, your total of 11 or more years of professional experience across all jobs was the strongest influence pushing the prediction toward leaving. Employees with this much overall experience are relatively uncommon among those the model expects to stay. Second, your 1 to 5 years in your current role also strongly pointed toward leaving. Most people the model predicts will stay have either much shorter or longer tenures here. Third, the fact that you have not received any other job offers while working here worked in the opposite direction, pulling the prediction slightly toward staying, though not enough to change the overall outlook.

Taken together, your long overall career and moderate time at this organization appear to signal that you may be ready for a significant next step elsewhere. The absence of external offers provided only a small counterbalance.

Your organization should discuss your career goals openly with you and explore whether internal opportunities could meet your ambitions. You may also want to reflect on what would make you want to stay long-term. Addressing these points could either reduce the risk of departure or help you make a well-informed move. (218 words)
